lines.en: Sana’s visiting from Kumon-mi tonight. She does this a few times a year, apparently.
She says the bar is a pretty notable location over there now that she’s taken over.
I asked her how Sara’s been and she was reluctant to tell me anything.
Apparently that tie was severed the moment I ran off with a teenager and she just doesn’t like talking about me anymore.
I don’t blame her, of course. I just think it’s a little interesting how likely she’d be to go back on that opinion if it was her daughter I took to Aomori instead.
Tonight’s not about her, though. Tonight is about us.
It’s about how far we’ve come and how much we’ve changed. Where we are and where we’ve been.
And also the fact that this is apparently the anniversary of my wedding to Ayane.
Why Sana needs to be present for that, I don’t quite understand. But I’m glad to see her either way.
She looks far more familiar than I expected her to, though. But I imagine that’s just one more subconsciously inherited memory that I’d be better off not questioning.
Now please excuse me as I try to tune out this conversation so as to not let my mind wander further from this table than it’s meant to be.
: What about the girls from the second dorm? Have you seen any of them lately? Or did most of them move away too?
: Weirdly enough, it’s Tsuneyo I see the most out of everyone these days. That’s really just because my apartment is close to Tojo Ramen though. She doesn’t get out very much from what I understand.
: Oh! Yasu too. She opened her own church-slash-charity organization thing and she comes by to post fliers sometimes. She’s, like...completely transformed since high school.
: I assume that means she’s not being led around on a leash by Touka anymore then?
: I don’t even think they talk. I see Touka on TV sometimes, though. Apparently her family got wrapped up in some sort of scandal shortly after she took over.
: Which means that I think I am somehow now the most successful business owner from our class! Bet nobody expected that.
: You haven’t heard from Ami, have you?
: Oh boy. Here we go again.
: Akira...we promised we wouldn’t talk about anything sad or depressing tonight. Remember?

: I don’t need an in-depth rundown on her existence. I just want to know if she’s still around and it seems like Sana’s up-to-date on everything going on over there on account of what she hears at work.
: Well, sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but I don’t know anything about what’s going on with her.
: Why not just call her yourself if you’re that curious. You still have her contact info, don’t you?
: That’s what I told him as well. But Akira is worried that she might, uhh...interfere when it comes to things with Himawari. And she’s obviously the top priority now.
: Awwww! Akira! To think you of all people would become such a softie makes me feel all warm and fuzzy inside. It gives me hope that perhaps it isn’t too late for me to change either.
: What, are you the evil one now then?
: Define “evil.” Because it’s not like I’m fucking an entire high school. I do occasionally overcharge people I find annoying, though.
: Oh, is that why the bar is so successful now?
: Of course not. The bar is so successful because it is owned and operated by an adorable, petite, black-haired angel who everyone loves and admires.
: Oh, so Sara’s still involved after all then?
: BIG WORDS FOR SOMEONE WHO ONLY LASTED THIRTY SECONDS WITH ME LAST TIME, FUCKER!
: On our anniversary? Really?
: Ahem. I apologize for my sudden outburst.
: But, in my defense, you were there too. And you are my best friend, so surely you will vouch for me so we can join forces and make fun of your husband together.
: Here’s a better idea! Why don’t we just change topics entirely and talk about something happier than what we ultimately ran away from?! Right, darling?
: But the only thing Akira is interested in these days is his daughter. And if I have to hear you guys brag about her anymore, I think I’m going to vomit.
: Just have one of your own! Then you can move to Aomori too and she can be Hima-chan’s friend. She needs more of those. She’s too much of a homebody these days.
: Oh, sure. I’ll just have a baby with no one and then ignore the fifteen year age gap between her and your daughter while uprooting my entire life. That makes perfect sense, Ayane.
: Act soon or it will be a sixteen year age gap.
: Yeah, that’s too big of a difference for them to be friends. At that point, it would make more sense for them to just elope and have a kid of their own.
: Come to think of it, are you even seeing anybody right now? Do you even want kids, Sana?
: No. What the hell would I do with one of those? Parenting seems horrible. I don’t want that much responsibility.
: Neither did Akira and you see what he’s become. Hima-chan’s his phone wallpaper and everything now.
: Sorry, is this supposed to be persuasive? Because it’s really just disgusting me more.
: Well, surely you at least have a boyfriend. Right?
: Define “boyfriend.”
: Someone you have slept with more than once who makes you happy.
: Oh. Then yeah, I guess I’m dating your husband. I sure hope this doesn’t ruin our friendship.
: Come on. That was funny.
: You’re terminally single, aren’t you?
: Ayane, I don’t want a boyfriend. I’m enjoying my life the way it is.
: Not everybody needs to settle down and have kids. Just because that’s what made you guys happy doesn’t mean it’s what’s right for me.
: I just worry about you. I don’t like how far away you are now. I can’t keep an eye on you anymore.
: You could see me a lot more if you actually came to visit, you know. You don’t really intend to keep Himawari away from Kumon-mi forever, do you?
: I do. Because I’m not going back and I can’t keep an eye on her if I’m not there.
: Sounds like a job for Aunt Sana. Don’t worry, Akira. I’ll give her the grand tour of the land that brought her parents together.
: I would sooner throw her off a cliff than hand her over to you.
: THIRTY SECONDS! THAT’S NOT ENOUGH TO MAKE ME FEEL ANYTHING!
: Okay! Well, I’m going back to the salad bar. Do you need another beer while I’m up? Sana’s paying tonight, so you should say yes even if that one is still full.
: I’ll take ten. Thanks. And if you could call home to check in on Himawari while you’re over there-
: Akira. She is fine. You are obsessed.
: You say that like she’s not your phone wallpaper as well.
: Good point. I suppose it wouldn’t hurt to just see how she’s doing. I’ll tell her you said hi.
: Be right back! Don’t kill each other while I’m gone, please!
Ayane scurries out of sight and, suddenly, I’m face-to-face in isolation with a different aspect of my past for the first time since I woke up here.
It’s one more aspect that’s changed dramatically, though. Much like everything else in life.
And while I want nothing more than to sit here and reflect on how time changes us, I know that moments like this will be so sparing from here on out that I’d be foolish to not capitalize on it.
I imagine Sana feels the same as she’s the one who breaks the silence before I have the chance to.
: You two are still just as in love as you were when I met you, huh?
: I wouldn’t run away with just anyone, you know.
: Ever wish it was me?
: What?
: I’m asking you — do you ever wish you ran away with me instead?
: It’s just a question, Akira. You can say no and it won’t hurt my feelings.
: Then no. I don’t.
: Good. That was the right answer. You belong with Ayane. You wouldn’t want to do something that would tear your family apart, after all.
: You’re being weird and scheming and I don’t like it. Is this you trying to flirt or something? Because it’s making me really uncomfortable.
: Why? You don’t think I’m trying to win you back, do you?
: Saying it that way makes it sound like you actually had me at some point.
: Maybe in some other world, I did.
: It’s always been Ayane in this one, though...with the rest of us fighting a losing battle.
: I really am happy for you, Akira. Your daughter is beautiful. And I think it’s cute how proud and...obsessed you are when it comes to her.
: It is, in every single way, a perfectly happy ending.
: But I imagine it must also feel a little sudden, huh?
: Like, one minute, you were in high school. And the next, you were so deep into the future that you barely had time to stop and ask yourself how you got there.
: Where does the time go? How did this happen? Who even am I? Questions like that.
: Sound familiar?
: What’s the matter? Cat got your tongue all of a sudden?
: Sana...do you...
: If you’re going to ask if I know something, don’t bother. I’m just as lost now as I was back then.
: And that’s assuming anything can ever really be known about all of this in the first place. What with the rules always changing and...things of that effect.
: I’ve thought about it, though.
: About if it was me.
: About what city we’d have gone to or what the color of our daughter’s eyes would be.
: It’s not because I’m jealous, though. Or even that I like you.
: It’s just different. And it’s possible. And you never really know what direction life is going to take you in.
: But an interesting thought to think is about how there might be a world for all of those things. How, somewhere out there, that might have happened.
: I wonder how that Sana feels. How that Akira feels. And if he loves what we created even half as much as what he loves here.
: Well, I can’t say that’s impossible, but...I can’t picture it, Sana.
: And...yeah. It was...sudden. All of this. Like a switch was flipped inside of me and everything went from terrible to amazing in the blink of an eye.
: And now you keep worrying that the switch is going to be flipped again and that all of it will go away?
: Exactly. It’s the second-to-last thing I think of before I fall asleep every night now.
: The last being-
: You know exactly what the last thing is. And something tells me you also know how worried I am that I won’t ever stop feeling this way.
: What, like you’re standing on a rug that someone’s trying to yank out from under you?
: Exactly. But why do you know that? You’re just a bartender now. We barely even see each other anymore. So why do you understand how I feel?
: Beats me. I think the answer is wedged somewhere between dream logic and survival instinct, though.
: Either that or it’s just the wine talking. I always say a little more than I want to when I’m drunk.
: You should drink more too, Akira. Tonight’s a celebration after all. Of you reaching the good ending.
: Those are always bittersweet when it comes to dating sims, though. Like you can’t help but feel bad for the all the heroines that wound up losing.
: Especially the ones directly tied to the winner — who get to sit back and watch as infinite joy so easily and constantly eludes them.
: I don’t really know what you want me to say.
: Nothing, really.
: It’s fine if you just look at me.
: I can imagine the rest.
: Okay! I’m back.
: Sorry — that was all I was able to carry.
: I spoke to Hima-chan too. She just got back from piano lessons.
: Piano lessons? Since when does she play piano?
: She just started, but she’s already really good! We bought her a keyboard as an early Christmas present and she’s been totally hooked on it lately.
: Just out of curiosity, is there anything she can’t do? Because it feels like she has a brand new hobby every time I hear about her.
: She can’t play mahjong.
: What a specific answer to just have locked and loaded like that. I guess you’re not wrong, though?
: She’ll learn eventually. Mahjong’s for old people and her father is basically a senior citizen now. It’s only a matter of time until you pick it up, Akira.
: How the hell am I going to drink all of these?
: You’ll figure it out. I just hope you don’t get so drunk that something crazy and inappropriate happens between all three of us again. That sure would suck, wouldn’t it?
: I’m like one more unwanted advance away from just finding you a boyfriend myself so we won’t have to put up with this anymore.
Sana winds up being the only one to get drunk tonight, which makes it all the more convenient that we decided to hold our get-together in her hotel’s penthouse bar.
And while she tries to drag us inside for another more physical reunion once we escort her back to her room, Ayane and I aren’t about to leave Himawari home alone through the night.
